items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The `netloc = f'{auth}@{netloc}'` line is clear, but unlike the reference it has no comment explaining that parse_url's netloc drops auth. The rebuild_proxies rewrite in sessions.py is readable, though nothing explains why the behaviour changed.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Out-of-scope changes: rebuild_proxies in sessions.py was rewritten to use `select_proxy`, and `get_auth_from_url` gained `or ''` fallbacks. The project context says no changes to session proxy handling are needed. It also edited the existing tests/test_utils.py.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: requests 2.27 still supports Python 2.7, so the f-string in utils.py stops the module importing there. rebuild_proxies now sets Proxy-Authorization when only a username is given (`if username:`), which changes behaviour beyond the fix.

items.name: prepend_scheme_if_needed public behaviour unchanged otherwise
items.name_zh: prepend_scheme_if_needed 其他公开行为不变
items.evidence: The signature is unchanged and auth comes from parse_url's `auth` field, with no urllib3 or Python-version special-casing, so no-auth behaviour is preserved on Python 3. But the `f'{auth}@{netloc}'` syntax breaks the function on Python 2.7, which this release still supports.
